cost: Free (no fee); unpaid placement — students earn credits, not wages. Some employers may offer an honorarium or help with expenses, but that is not standard.
description: Ministry-approved program letting secondary students earn high-school credits through a work placement in the community, combining in-class learning with hands-on work experience. A co-op course is monitored by a co-op teacher and linked to a related curriculum course. Up to 2 co-op credits can count toward compulsory OSSD requirements; there is no limit on optional co-op credits.
how_to_access: For Grade 11/12: choose co-op during course selection, or talk to the school guidance counsellor / co-op department. The school arranges and assesses the placement; the student may also find a placement in collaboration with the co-op teacher. In Bowmanville this means Owen's own high school (Durham District School Board or Durham Catholic District School Board — which school Owen attends was not stated, so do not assert it).
name: High-school Cooperative Education (co-op)
notes: Co-op is the single most useful route for Owen: it is work experience during school hours, earns OSSD credits, and a good placement often turns into a paid after-school/weekend job with the same employer. It is unpaid by design — do not present co-op as paid employment. Summer-school and night-school co-op exist in some boards; a paid job can sometimes count for co-op credits — check with the school.
who_for: Grade 11 and 12 students who have completed Grade 10, in any pathway (apprenticeship, college, university, workplace). Typically a 2-credit (half-day) or 4-credit (full-day) placement for one semester.

description: School-to-work program letting high-school students explore and begin training in a skilled trade while earning high-school credits, through a co-op placement in an apprenticeable trade (e.g. automotive service technician, hairstylist, general carpenter). Participants may register as apprentices and start accumulating apprenticeship hours/competencies while still in high school. OYAP-FAST is an accelerated stream (from September 2025) letting Grade 11/12 students do more apprenticeship learning and earn an OYAP-FAST seal on their OSSD.
how_to_access: Talk to the school guidance counsellor or co-op education teacher; contact the school board's OYAP recruiter (listed on the ontario.ca page). Students must complete an OYAP Participant Form before their first co-op placement in a trade. Accelerated Level 1 OYAP (college-delivered trade school) requires an application and interview, applied for in Grade 11.
name: Ontario Youth Apprenticeship Program (OYAP)
notes: Only relevant if Owen wants a skilled trade. The OYAP page on ontario.ca was opened and verified directly. For Bowmanville, the recruiter is the one for Owen's school board (DDSB or DCDSB) — the board was not confirmed, so no recruiter name/contact is listed here.
who_for: High-school students aged 15+, enrolled part-time or full-time, in Grade 11 or 12 (or equivalent), with at least 14 credits earned. Students who completed Grade 10 may participate in the summer before Grade 11 — check with the school.

cost: Free to the student/parent — dual-credit courses are funded through the School-College-Work Initiative (SCWI); the Durham College page states students experience college 'at no cost to the parent or student'.
description: High-school students take a college course taught by a college instructor and earn BOTH a high-school credit and a college credit that may count toward a future diploma, degree or apprenticeship. Durham College delivers 2,000+ dual credits a year with partner boards including Durham District School Board and Durham Catholic District School Board. Options include college-delivered, team-taught, and OYAP dual credits. The Centre for Success (School Within a College) is a full-semester Grade 12 exit program at the Oshawa/Whitby campuses where students finish their OSSD and earn a Durham College dual credit.
how_to_access: Through the high school guidance department / the board's dual-credit lead. See earndualcredits.ca for offerings by board. Centre for Success: application for February 2027 (Semester 2) was listed as open on the DDSB page — for Grade 12 students with 24+ credits who are within a semester of graduating.
name: Durham College — Dual Credit Programs (SCWI)
notes: Most useful for Owen in Grade 11/12. Note the Centre for Success stream is an exit/graduation program (24+ credits), not a general enrichment option — do not present it as open to all grades. No 2026-27 dual-credit course list for Bowmanville specifically was confirmed; offerings vary by semester and board.
who_for: Secondary students in partner boards (DDSB, DCDSB, Kawartha Pine Ridge, PVNCCDSB), particularly those in SHSM or OYAP, at risk of not graduating, or exploring a post-secondary pathway.

cost: Outreach workshops are paid, not free: Inside Engineering $35 per workshop or $150 for all five; virtual high-school workshops $50 CAD each (per the Ontario Tech pages).
description: Ontario Tech University (Oshawa) runs Engineering Outreach programs for high-school students, including Inside Engineering (Grades 9-12, hands-on workshops across engineering disciplines, in person and virtual) and Future Leaders in Training (Grades 9-12, technology/leadership), plus virtual curriculum-linked workshops for Grades 9-12. These are enrichment/outreach, not employment and not credit-bearing.
how_to_access: Register via the Engineering Outreach high-school programs page. Inside Engineering ran Nov 2-6, 2026 and registration is now CLOSED; Future Leaders in Training is also listed CLOSED. Watch the page for the next intake.
name: Ontario Tech University — Engineering Outreach (high-school programs)
notes: NO DUAL-CREDIT PROGRAM AT ONTARIO TECH WAS FOUND in this research — do not claim one exists. The university's high-school offering is outreach/enrichment only, and the 2026-27 flagship programs are already closed for registration. Included because it is local (Oshawa campus) and useful for exposure, not for job hunting.
who_for: Ontario secondary students, Grades 9-12, interested in engineering/STEM.

cost: Not published on the Clarington lifeguarding page — fees and dates are via clarington.net/BeActive. Historical Clarington rates (2019-2023 documents, now stale) were roughly $160-$250 per course; DO NOT quote those as current. A 25% discount applies if the student took any Clarington swimming/lifesaving/leadership course in the past 3 years (per the current Clarington page).
description: Lifesaving Society lifeguard pathway: Bronze Star (optional, 10 hrs) → Bronze Medallion (13+ by exam date or Bronze Star; 400 m timed swim) → Bronze Cross (13+ by course end; requires Bronze Medallion + Emergency/Standard — now Basic/Intermediate — First Aid; 20 hrs; assistant-lifeguard award and prerequisite for National Lifeguard) → National Lifeguard (15+; requires Bronze Cross + Intermediate/Standard First Aid with CPR-C; 40 hrs; the legal certificate for lifeguarding public pools in Ontario).
how_to_access: Locally through the Municipality of Clarington (Bowmanville): lifeguarding/leadership courses at Clarington facilities — register via clarington.net/BeActive. Clarington also hires Assistant Lifeguards/Assistant Instructors (minimum: current Bronze Cross) and Lifeguards (National Lifeguard) part-time — see the Municipality's part-time jobs page.
name: Bronze Cross / Lifeguard pathway (Lifesaving Society)
notes: Strongest certification route for Owen: Bronze Cross can be done at 13+, National Lifeguard at 15, and Clarington itself hires teens with these awards for local pool jobs — no car needed if the pool is in Bowmanville. Costs are the gap: current Clarington fees were not published on the page checked and must be looked up on BeActive before quoting any price.
who_for: Strong swimmers aged 13+ (Bronze Medallion/Cross) and 15+ (National Lifeguard).

cost: Provider-dependent: examples found were $130-$180 for Standard/Intermediate First Aid with CPR-C/AED (e.g. $145 at one Red Cross training partner; $130-$140 at another). Durham First Aid (Oshawa, Red Cross Training Partner) lists a $5-$1,050 price range across all its courses — its specific Standard/Intermediate First Aid price was not confirmed. Do not quote a single price.
description: Two-day (about 14 hours) first-aid course covering CPR (Level C: adults, children, infants) and AED, plus injuries, sudden medical emergencies and environmental emergencies. Certification is valid 3 years. NOTE: as of June 22, 2026 the WSIB modernized first-aid program renamed 'Standard First Aid' to 'Intermediate First Aid' and 'Emergency First Aid' to 'Basic First Aid' in Ontario — course listings may use either name.
how_to_access: Through a Red Cross Training Partner or Lifesaving Society provider. Local option: Durham First Aid Inc., Oshawa (Canadian Red Cross Training Partner, WSIB-approved, offers youth courses). Also available through the Municipality of Clarington (WSIB-approved first-aid provider) alongside Bronze Cross. Ontario courses require an in-class component with hands-on CPR practice/evaluation.
name: Standard First Aid (now Intermediate First Aid) + CPR-C/AED
notes: Age: a Red Cross training partner (Durham First Aid) states there is NO age restriction on Basic/Intermediate First Aid, but individual providers set their own minima (13 or 14 seen in listings) — confirm with the chosen provider before booking for Owen. This certificate is a prerequisite for Bronze Cross (Emergency/Basic level suffices) and National Lifeguard (Standard/Intermediate level required), and is valued by employers for camp, recreation, childcare and customer-service roles.
who_for: Anyone wanting workplace first-aid certification; no Red Cross age restriction on Basic/Intermediate First Aid per the local training partner, but providers may set a minimum (13-14).

cost: Online accredited courses about $25-$50 (examples: SafeCheck $24.88; Probe It $49.95). In-person public-health-unit courses about $40-$62 (examples: Lambton $40 class / $10 exam; Southwestern $62.15). Prices vary by provider; no single official price.
description: Food-handler training under Section 32 of O. Reg. 493/17 (Food Premises): every food premises must have at least one certified food handler or supervisor on site during every hour of operation. The course covers safe food handling; the exam is multiple choice with a 70% pass mark; the certificate is valid 5 years and is recognized by all Ontario public health units, including Durham Region Health Department.
how_to_access: Online through a Ministry-recognized provider (e.g. SafeCheck, Probe It, In Good Hands), or in person through a public health unit. Durham Region Health Department is Owen's local health unit — its own course schedule/fees were NOT confirmed in this research and should be checked directly before quoting them.
name: Food Handler Certification (Ontario)
notes: No minimum age was found in any source checked — age eligibility is UNVERIFIED; confirm with the chosen provider (a teen can generally take it, but do not state that as fact). Useful for grocery, fast-food, cafe and restaurant jobs — the most likely first-job employers for Owen.
who_for: Anyone handling food in an Ontario food premises; commonly required or preferred by food-service employers. Minimum age unverified.

cost: $44.95 CAD for the Smart Serve Full Online Training Program; $24.95 CAD for the Smart Serve Retail program (retail stores only). Both non-refundable, non-transferable. Recertification $29.95 before expiry. Verified directly on smartserve.ca, 2026-11-16.
description: Ontario's mandatory responsible alcohol service training, approved by the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO). The Full course (4-5 hours, self-paced online) covers anyone selling, serving, delivering or sampling liquor; the Retail course (1.5-2 hours) is for retail settings only. Final test is proctored online (webcam + government photo ID), 33 questions (Full) / 20 questions (Retail), 80% to pass. Certificate valid 5 years.
how_to_access: Online only at smartserve.ca. Training is self-paced, 24/7.
name: Smart Serve (Ontario)
notes: CONFIRMED NOT USABLE UNTIL 18: the minimum age to sell, serve, handle or deliver alcohol in Ontario is 18 (AGCO / Liquor Licence and Control Act), and the legal drinking age is 19. Some providers say training itself can be taken at any age, others list 18+ to enrol — either way Owen cannot work with alcohol until 18, so do not list Smart Serve as a near-term option for him. Flag it as a 'when you turn 18' item only.
who_for: Anyone 18+ who sells, serves, delivers or samples alcohol in Ontario. NOT for Owen until he turns 18.
